newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 6.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 6.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Thursday:

* On Wednesday, the Dow Jones industrial average closed down 86.58 points, or 1.27 percent, at 6,746.90 after losing more than 120 points in a late sell-off of market-leading technology shares. The drop in the stock market came after Federal Reserve policy-makers decided to leave interest rates steady at the end of a two-day meeting.

* Indonesia expects its inflation rate to drop below six percent in the current fiscal year ending March 31, bringing it close to the five percent target of its five-year development plan, officials said on Wednesday.

* On Wednesday, the Jakarta Composite Index rose 6.53 points, or 0.96 percent, to close at 686.86 points as the market received strong support from overseas buying of certain heavyweights, brokers said.
* On Thursday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,376.50/77.00 in early trading against the opening of 2,377.50/78.00.

* Indonesia's largest noodle maker PT Indofood Sukses Makmur on report it has submitted a registration statement to the capital market supervisory agency (Bapepam) for a 1.259 trillion rupiah rights issue offering with 4:1 terms at the price of 3,300 rupiah-4,000 rupiah per share.
* Fishery firm PT Daya Guna Samudera on media report that Indonesian government had issued a licence to to the firm to import second-hand fishing vessels.
* Department store operator PT Ramayana Lestari Sentosa following report that its net profit in 1996 would reach 67 billion rupiah, slightly higher than the company's previously announced target.

* Tambang Timah on announcement it posted a net profit of 156.6 billion rupiah in 1996 against 134.5 billion rupiah in 1995 coupled with market speculation that it is likely to participate in Busang gold project.

* PT Multipolar Corp after shareholder approval on Thursday of its plan to take a 50.1 percent controlling interest in retailer PT Matahari Putra Prima. Also on market speculation of a possible stock split.
* PT Barito Pacific on rumours that new investors may enter Indonesia's largest plywood firm.
